message.content:
In Texas, tenants have several statutory protections and responsibilities under the Texas Property Code and related laws. Here’s a quick overview of your key rights: | Category | What You’re Entitled To | |----------|------------------------| | **Security Deposit** | • Landlords may charge up to one month’s rent (or two if the lease is for a furnished unit).
• Must be returned within 30 days after you move out, minus any lawful deductions. | | **Habitability** | • Landlord must keep the premises safe, sanitary, and in good repair (e.g., plumbing, heating, structural integrity). | | **Right to Quiet Enjoyment** | • Landlord cannot disturb your peaceful use of the property without proper notice. | | **Notice Requirements** | • For non‑payment of rent: 3‑day written notice before eviction.
• For lease termination: 30‑day notice for month‑to‑month agreements; 60‑day for longer leases. | | **Eviction Process** | • Must follow the court process; landlords cannot forcibly remove you or lock you out. | | **Repair & Deduct / Rent Withhold** | • If landlord fails to fix major problems, you may withhold rent or pay repairs yourself and deduct from rent (but only after giving notice and following procedure). | | **Privacy** | • Landlord must give reasonable notice (usually 24 hours) before entering the unit, except in emergencies. | | **Discrimination Protections** | • Protected against discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, etc. | | **Lease Terms** | • Lease must be in writing if it lasts longer than one year.
• Certain clauses (e.g., “no pets” or “no smoking”) are enforceable if clearly stated. | | **Rent Control** | • Texas has no statewide rent control; rent increases are governed by lease terms and local ordinances. | ### Practical Tips 1. **Document Everything** – Keep copies of all communications, receipts, and photos of any damage or maintenance issues. 2. **Know Your Lease** – Read it carefully; many disputes arise from misunderstandings about what’s covered. 3. **Use Written Notices** – Send notices via certified mail or email with read receipt to establish proof. 4. **Seek Legal Aid** – If you face eviction or other disputes, consider contacting a local tenant advocacy group or legal aid office. If you need help drafting a lease or a notice, let me know and I can generate a template for you.
